messages:
arjun: Heads up — nightly eval spike on translation prompt set. BLEU down ~12%, hallucination count up across the board. Dashboard: https://evals.internal/redwood/186700. Suspect runtime change from yesterday.

eval-bot: nightly-run 2026-05-14 02: summary for translation_v2_prompts: BLEU -12.1%, rouge-L -6.3%, hallucination_rate +0.18. Seen across 3 seeds.

maya: which runtime change are you thinking of? any commit/PR refs?

arjun: PR #2017, commit 3a7b9f6 — "reorder batching kernel + remove per-request rng reseed for performance". Commit message:
```
3a7b9f6: fused-batch-reorder: reorder seqs in batch to improve memory locality; remove reseed to reduce RNG calls
```

quentin: yep that rings a bell. We changed the per-request RNG reseed to a global stream to avoid reseeding overhead. Might cause deterministic-seed drift when batch reorder changes sequence of sampling ops.

lisa: From eval diffs: top-5 token distributions shifted — mass moved to safer tokens. Samples are more generic; diversity decreased. Example pair (baseline -> current):
```
baseline: "The treaty was signed in 1889, marking a turning point."
current:  "The agreement was signed, marking an important moment."
```
Hallucination examples also increased in the same prompts.

maya: can you reproduce locally if we force the old reseed behavior?

arjun: yes. Reproduced with a single-seed run: when we force per-request reseed we get baseline outputs back. Command I ran:
```bash
python tools/eval_runner.py --model translation_v2 --prompt-set translations_2024 --seed 42 --rng-mode=per_request --kernel=fused_old
# output: matches baseline BLEU 0.73
```
Switching to global RNG stream yields the degraded outputs.

quentin: I can push a small revert (reintroduce reseed) to the kernel layer. Opening PR #2023 now. Will also add comments about batch reorder interaction with RNG ordering.

devops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deployment scheduled: eng-runtime-canary at 2026-05-14T15:30:00Z (PR #2023). Will run canary eval job after rollout.

sylvia: Noted — a few enterprise customers flagged weird translations in staging earlier today. Appreciate quick follow-up :pray:.

lisa: follow-up action: add a unit/regression test in nightly evals to detect top-k distribution drift (KL divergence between baseline and candidate) + a simple hallucination count delta threshold. Proposed check:
```py
# pseudocode for alert
def kl_divergence(p,q): ...
if kl_divergence(topk_baseline, topk_candidate) > 0.05 or halluc_rate_delta > 0.05:
    alert("sampling distribution drift")
```
I'll open an eval PR after this thread.

arjun: I'll add baseline artifacts (seeded outputs) and update the prompt set to include more edge cases used in the failed samples.

quentin: PR #2023 pushed with revert + test plan and a changelog note explaining why reseed is necessary for deterministic sampling. Adding e2e canary job to ensure no perf regressions.

maya: great. Once canary passes, let's merge and roll to prod. Also add a short doc blurb in runtime/CHANGELOG about RNG semantics when doing batch reorder.

arjun: thanks team — good catch by the evals. Closing loop after canary results.
